top news.title: Sources: Trump delayed signing the AI EO because “he just hates regulation”; there were questions about the EO giving the Treasury Department a leading role

tweets.author: @dashaburns
tweets.text: NEW: Trump told me in an interview today that he “was hearing concerns” about the AI executive order but was also “seeing the concerns myself.”  “I have concerns about it, and I don't want to approve anything until it's done properly,” he said.

tweets.author: @cheyennehaslett
tweets.text: Andy Stone, spokesperson for Meta, says Mark Zuckerberg didn't talk to Trump until after the president made the call to abrupty pull yesterday's AI executive order: “Mark didn't speak to the president until after the event had already been canceled.”  Elon Musk earlier today said he also didn't speak to the president about pulling yesterday's scheduled AI executive order until after it happened.

tweets.author: @mikeisaac
tweets.text: interesting media study on how many different versions of “why the AI exec order wasnt signed” are going around right now and who gets to save face depending on where the story landed [image]

sub_items.title: Sources: Trump postponed AI EO signing after talking to David Sacks and others, and told staff the EO is not moving forward after calls with Musk and Zuckerberg
Sources: David Sacks told President Trump that federal reviews of AI models before release would slow down innovation and hurt the US in its AI race with China

top news.title: Meta releases Forum, a Reddit-like standalone app for Facebook Groups, with a feed showing Group conversations and an AI-powered “Ask” feature, on iOS

tweets.author: @mattnavarra
tweets.text: Update Just received this comment about Forum from the Meta via email: “We test lots of new products publicly to see what people find interesting and useful to their experiences across our apps.” - Meta Spokesperson

tweets.author: @millsbaker
tweets.text: Just yesterday I mentioned FB's habit of spinning out (and later reintegrating) products! Features like Groups are bigger than many companies, easily justify their own apps, but also pale compared to “the overall platform” and get reabsorbed later.

tweets.author: @milkkarten
tweets.text: interest-based algorithms have rooted out the “social” in social media so now those same platforms are creating new apps to address problems of their own making

sub_items.title: Reddit stock fell 5%+ on Friday after Meta launched a standalone app for online forums, called Forum; Reddit's stock is now down almost 40% this year
